findings.text: The classifier's one non-order discriminating condition is unpinned, and it is the condition that governs the cohort's own reason string. `if reason and reason != _COMPOSE_CAP_REASON:` excludes the literal 'compose claim-attempt cap reached'. Triggering input: delete ` and reason != _COMPOSE_CAP_REASON`. Measured in a /dev/shm copy of HEAD: the file reports 6 passed exit 0 (mutation-cap-reason-guard-dropped.log), while every parked row whose last_error IS that literal moves from cause_not_recorded (or compose_not_applicable, when a category is present) to attempt_budget_exhausted. Both are declared members, so nothing in the write path or the closed-set tests shows the difference - the exact silent member-to-member reclassification this node exists to prevent. That literal is what _CAP_UNDISPOSED_QUERY is handed as cap_reason at graph_ops.py:11617, so plausibly most of the live cohort carries it. No case in the file constructs it: verified that the string appears in none of BRANCH_CASES or ADJACENT_PAIR_CASES, and classify({'last_error': _COMPOSE_CAP_REASON}) -> 'cause_not_recorded' today (signal-liveness-probe.log). Fix: two cases - the cap reason alone must stay cause_not_recorded, and the cap reason with node_category=geometry must stay compose_not_applicable.

ADJACENT_PAIR_CASES is a hardcoded list of four with nothing asserting it still covers the classifier's adjacencies, so the enumeration decays the first time a branch is inserted. Triggering input: add any sixth top-level condition returning an existing disposition on a signal no case sets. Measured by inserting `if str(evidence.get('dd_status') or '').strip() == 'obsolescent': return 'upstream_quantity_removed'` between the produced and removed branches in a /dev/shm copy of HEAD: two new adjacencies appear, neither pinned, and the file reports 6 passed exit 0 (mutation-new-branch-inserted-unpinned-adjacency.log). BRANCH_CASES has the same shape - a new branch returning an existing disposition is reached by no case and the coverage test still passes. The node's own comment anticipates exactly this edit (it is the stated reason for keying cases by precedence rather than by branch number) but builds no detector for it. Fix: derive the count from the source rather than restating it - assert the number of return statements in inspect.getsource(graph_ops.classify_parked_source) equals len(BRANCH_CASES), and that len(ADJACENT_PAIR_CASES) covers positions-1.

BRANCH_CASES is keyed by the disposition each input should return, but no test asserts that correspondence - the pre-existing pair is weaker than its own keying implies. test_every_branch_returns_a_declared_disposition checks membership only; test_the_representative_inputs_cover_the_whole_declared_set checks set equality only. Triggering input: permute two return values inside the recorded-cause block, so a vocabulary-gap reason returns attempt_budget_exhausted and any other cause returns vocabulary_gap. Measured: 2 failed, 4 passed, exit 1, and BOTH reds are the node's NEW pair-3 cases - the two pre-existing tests stay green under a permutation that inverts the classifier's meaning for the whole cause branch (mutation-substring-outcomes-swapped.log). This is not a defect the node introduced and the new cases do incidentally catch it, but the cheap direct assertion is absent: one line, `assert graph_ops.classify_parked_source(dict(evidence)) == disposition` per BRANCH_CASES item.

Two published figures do not reconcile, in a record whose whole point is a branch enumeration. First, 'The classifier has five terminating branches' appears here, in the plan comment and in the manifest's evidence_inputs; the source has SIX terminating returns and six dispositions, and the test file's own docstring reasons about 'a seventh branch'. Five is the number of top-level POSITIONS, which is what the pair arithmetic needs, so the conclusion (four adjacent pairs) is right and the premise as written is wrong - a reader re-deriving the enumeration, which is what this record asks for, reaches a different number. Second, the commit body and the plan comment report the negative control as '2 failed, 5 passed, exit 1' beside 'the file reports 2 passed before the change and 6 passed after it'; 2+5=7 against a 6-test file. The seventh item is the node's own test_scratch_origin.py, collected in the same run (confirmed: /tmp/npark_negative_control.log reports 'collected 7 items' and lists it) and named in neither message. Re-running the identical mutation over the file alone gives 2 failed, 4 passed (mutation-pair3-category-above-cause.log). The figure is honest and unreconcilable as published. Separately, manifest orientation_base_sha 44650230ce9b585c83add9e5a547ee94121cec1f does not exist - `git cat-file -e` returns 'bad object'; the real parent is 44650230ce9b585c83add9b5a547ee94121cec1f, one hex digit different, and the abbreviated form in baseline_suite.revision resolves, so a short-form check passes while a long-form check errors.

That is the same member-to-member silent reclassification the node exists to prevent, on the reason string that the cohort's own query passes as cap_reason at graph_ops.py:11617 - so plausibly most of the cohort. No case in the file constructs it (verified: the literal appears in none of BRANCH_CASES or ADJACENT_PAIR_CASES). Third, BRANCH_CASES is keyed by the disposition its input should return and nothing asserts that correspondence: test_every_branch_returns_a_declared_disposition checks membership only, and the coverage test checks set equality only. Permuting the two outcomes inside the cause block leaves BOTH pre-existing tests green - measured, mutation-substring-outcomes-swapped.log is 2 failed 4 passed and both reds are new cases. One line (`assert classify(dict(ev)) == key` per item) would close it.
justifications.evidence: The base and head figures reproduce exactly. I rebuilt HEAD by git archive into /dev/shm plus the five gitignored generated files and ran the file there: 6 passed exit 0, collected 6 (scratch-baseline.log), matching after_suite. The negative control log at /tmp/npark_negative_control.log is well formed - its first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim ('in a scratch copy outside the repository, move the node-category condition ... above the recorded-cause condition ...'), it names the two red cases by id, and they are exactly the two that pin the recorded-cause precedence. The second control log backs the fourth-pair claim at 1 failed 5 passed. The mutation ran only in a scratch tree and the node added a scratch-origin probe asserting the imported module resolved under it, which is the right instinct. Docked six for two reporting defects. First, orientation_base_sha in the manifest is 44650230ce9b585c83add9e5a547ee94121cec1f and NO SUCH OBJECT EXISTS: `git cat-file -e` returns 'bad object'. The real parent of 7c698663a is 44650230ce9b585c83add9b5a547ee94121cec1f - one hex digit different (add9e5a vs add9b5a). baseline_suite.revision carries the same corrupt value abbreviated to '44650230c', which DOES resolve, so a coordinator checking the short form sees green and a coordinator checking the long form sees a fatal error. Second, the commit body and the plan comment both report the negative control as '2 failed, 5 passed, exit 1' beside 'the file reports ... 6 passed after it'. Those cannot both describe the same file: 2+5=7. The seventh item is the node's own test_scratch_origin.py, collected in the same run and mentioned nowhere in either message; my own run of the identical mutation over the file alone is 2 failed, 4 passed. The figure is honest but unreconcilable as published. Minor: all four test_logs are /tmp paths and the 26 MB scratch copy is still sitting in /tmp, which is a shared allocation the repo guidance asks to keep small; the control also ran with rootdir /tmp and configfile /tmp/pyproject.toml (an unrelated 'reckon-plans' project that happens to sit there), so it inherited none of the repo's addopts - immaterial for this markerless file, but it is not the repo's pytest configuration.
justifications.fit: The change extends the file's existing idiom rather than starting a parallel one: a module-level dict of cases beside BRANCH_CASES, parametrised with ids taken from the keys, so a failure names the precedence it broke ('a recorded cause outranks the node category') instead of an index. Keying by precedence rather than by branch position is the right call and the comment says why. The docstring addition states the mechanism - first match wins, so one signal cannot see a reorder - which is the sentence a reader needs. It touches no source, so it cannot regress behaviour. TWO, both signals live in every case: I verified each case's two keys individually against the real classifier (signal-liveness-probe.log). All four are genuinely two-sided - {'produced':1} alone gives name_produced while {'lifecycle_status':'removed'} alone gives upstream_quantity_removed; removed alone vs {'last_error':'compose request timed out'} alone giving attempt_budget_exhausted; that same last_error alone vs {'node_category':'geometry'} alone giving compose_not_applicable; and the vocabulary-gap last_error alone giving vocabulary_gap vs {'node_category':'coordinate'} alone giving compose_not_applicable. No case has an inert signal, so none of them would pass under the inverted order. FOUR, the sub-branch question is handled correctly: vocabulary_gap and attempt_budget_exhausted sit under one outer condition and differ on a substring, so they are not an adjacent pair in the reorder sense - swapping them is not a reorder of the sequence - and the node rightly did not invent a fifth pair for them, instead crossing the pair-3 boundary once from each side. The substring discrimination IS pinned, though only as a side effect and only by the new cases: permuting the two returns under the cause block gives 2 failed 4 passed exit 1, both reds being the new pair-3 cases, with the two pre-existing tests green. Docked three. The 'five terminating branches' wording contradicts the file's own docstring ('a seventh branch') and the six returns in the source. And the module docstring presents ADJACENT_PAIR_CASES as the adjacency instrument while the fourth pair is actually held by a different test for a structural reason; nothing in the file records that, so a reader counting four pairs against four cases will conclude the mapping is one-to-one when it is three-plus-one.
justifications.goal_fidelity: VERDICT SOUND. The goal - the parked classifier's precedence is asserted - is met, and was verified here against the landed diff at the integrated head (8c6a38b20; 7c698663a is an ancestor), not taken from the report. ONE, the branch enumeration. I enumerated the classifier myself from graph_ops.py:11446-11457: six terminating returns across FIVE sequential top-level positions - produced, lifecycle_status==removed, the recorded-cause block (which splits on a substring into vocabulary_gap and attempt_budget_exhausted), node_category in {geometry,coordinate}, and the unconditional fallback. Five positions give FOUR adjacent pairs, which is exactly what the node claims. Every pair has a case: pairs 1-3 by the four new ADJACENT_PAIR_CASES (pair 3 twice, once per sub-branch of the cause block), and pair 4 by the pre-existing reachability test - correctly so, because the fallback is unconditional and has no signal of its own, so no two-signal case for it can exist. That is not a gap the node papered over; it is the only available instrument and the node measured it. THREE, every reordering, not just the one the node controlled. I ran all four adjacent transpositions in a scratch copy of HEAD at /dev/shm (logs mutation-pair1..pair4): pair 1 produced-below-removed 1 failed 5 passed exit 1; pair 2 removed-below-cause 1 failed 5 passed exit 1; pair 3 category-above-cause 2 failed 4 passed exit 1; pair 4 category-below-fallback 1 failed 5 passed exit 1 (the red test being test_the_representative_inputs_cover_the_whole_declared_set). Four of four reorderings go red, so the suite does not report a protection it withholds. This is also complete against arbitrary permutations, not only transpositions: any non-identity permutation has a minimal inversion, and a minimal inversion is necessarily adjacent, so a case per adjacent pair covers every reorder of the current branch set. Docked two for an enumeration wording error the node repeats in three places - the evidence record, the plan comment and evidence_inputs all say 'five terminating branches'. There are six terminating returns and six dispositions; five is the number of top-level POSITIONS. The arithmetic that matters (5 positions, 4 pairs) is right, but the file's own docstring reasons about 'a seventh branch', so the record contradicts the source it describes on the one count the done-when rests on.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 44650230ce9b585c83add9b5a547ee94121cec1f 7c698663a is exactly three files and exactly the three declared write paths, nothing else: tests/standard_names/test_parked_disposition_vocabulary.py, docs/plans/sn-lifecycle-integrity.html and docs/evidence/archive/sn-lifecycle-integrity-landed.html. 116 insertions, 1 deletion. The plan edit is a single worker-owned r-comment in the followups section that explicitly leaves the driving followup and the section's terminal state to coordinator adjudication; zero meta lines are touched. The commit is conventional with a subject AND a substantial body. A case-insensitive scan of the message for co-authored-by / generated with / claude / copilot returns 0 hits. The naming check over the test file for plan, phase, ticket and version labels is clean, and the file deliberately keys its cases by precedence rather than by branch number for exactly that reason. ruff check --no-cache on the test file: All checks passed. No branch created, nothing pushed, no source file modified - the node changed only tests and records, which is what a pin-the-behaviour node should do.
